gotchas: A cookie banner covers the page on a fresh profile: decline it first, or the fill targets nothing. Recorded from a completed signup by hand (#626); a proxy browser starts with an empty profile every run, so it re-arms each time.

Observed 2026-10-09 through the proxy: the email (input[name="susi_email"], submit with Enter) leads to 'Sign up for Dropbox' with First name (input[name="fname"]), Last name (input[name="lname"]), Password (input[type="password"], autocomplete new-password; #credential-autofill-hint no longer exists) and 'Agree and sign up'.
The cookie banner's Decline button sits in an untitled iframe (the second iframe on the page); iframe[src*=consent] matches nothing.

On 2026-10-09, three submits from the proxy's egress left the form disabled behind a spinner that never cleared, with no error, no detected challenge and no mail. Whether the account exists was not established.

Completed 2026-10-11 through the staging proxy (default egress): /register is now email-first (input[name=susi_email] + the page's submit 'Continue' — button[type=submit] is unique there, unlike text 'Continue'), then fname / lname / password and the single button[type=submit]. The identity first_name/last_name tokens must have values in the owner's identity: on 2026-10-11 an identity with no name filled empty and Dropbox answered 'Please enter your first name' (#778). With the name set, submit created the account with no challenge, no spinner and no email code, landing on the plan picker. The cookie banner did not need dismissing.
